=========== docs/faqs
Institutional Investors Summary by Investor Frequently Asked Questions How are ticker changes handled? The ticker is a unique identifier for a security. When a ticker changes we rewire the history for the updated ticker. When a company is delisted and its ticker is later reused by a different company, the active company keeps the ticker and the delisted company gets a number appended. Historical ticker changes are recorded in the actions table. In addition, we provide a permaticker in the tickers table that is Sharadar’s own unchanging and unique identifier for a security. Separate share classes of the same issuer receive separate permatickers. What does the tickers category field represent? Category combines SEC filing origin (Domestic form 10; ADR form 20; Canadian form 40) with instrument type (common stock, preferred, ETF, CEF, ETN, ETD, and related forms) and share-class role where relevant (Primary Class or Secondary Class). The current vocabulary is on the tickers table metadata. Institutional Investor is used for holdings_investor entity rows, not listed securities. There is no warrant category. Do you provide acquisition share/cash consideration? Yes. Cash and stock consideration for acquisitions and mergers is in the actions table. acquisitioncash is cash received per share (USD). acquisitionstock is the number of shares of the acquiring or surviving security received for each share of the acquired or non-surviving company. When both cash and stock were received, the two actions are additive. Contingent value rights are not included. When holders could elect cash or stock, acquisitionelectcash and acquisitionelectstock record the alternatives (one, not both). We estimate about 99% coverage of acquisition and merger consideration and are continuously improving that. Field-level detail is in the descriptions table where the table field equals actiontypes. Do you provide historical industry classifications? Yes. Historical SIC industry changes are in the actions table as sicchangefrom and sicchangeto (view them together). value is the SIC code and contraname is the industry title. sicchangefrom is the prior classification; sicchangeto is the new one as of that date. The current SIC is on the tickers table. Field-level detail is in the descriptions table where the table field equals actiontypes. How are company restatements handled within the fundamentals dataset? The fundamentals table keeps as-reported and restated financials as separate reporting dimensions. As-Reported (ARQ, ARY, ART) is a point-in-time view, time-indexed to the SEC form 10 filing date, and excludes restatements. That view is not rewritten when a later filing restates a prior period; the later filing creates a new observation. As-Reported is typically suitable for back-testing. Most-Recent Reported (MRQ, MRY, MRT) is time-indexed to the report period and is updated when a company restates prior periods. That view is typically suitable for assessing business performance after restatements for mergers or divestitures. Filter with dimension= to choose a view. For the POST example and more detail see Restatements on the fundamentals page. Do you provide historical changes to primary listing venues? Yes. Historical primary listing venue changes are in the actions table as exchangefrom and exchangeto (view them together). What is the easiest way to retrieve data? The easiest way to retrieve data is the bulk download method. This allows you to download entire tables in zipped CSV format with 5, 10 or full history depending on your preference and subscription permissions. The downloads are pre-prepared and available at a single click or API call. We also provide a REST API which allows you to filter for the precise data you want to retrieve, which is suitable in the event you want a limited amount of data. What corporate action adjustments are made to your price data? The stocks and funds tables provide EOD OHLCV data that is unadjusted; split-adjusted; and split, cash dividend and spinoff adjusted. Open, High, Low, Close and Volume are split-adjusted. CloseUnadj is unadjusted and can be used to impute unadjusted Open, High and Low (OpenUnadj = Open * CloseUnadj / Close). Tape-reported volume is the reciprocal: VolumeUnadj = Volume * Close / CloseUnadj. CloseAdj is split, cash dividend and spinoff adjusted and can be used to impute fully adjusted Open, High and Low. Volume is not adjusted for cash dividends or spinoffs. For more see this post . Is your data survivorship bias free? Yes, we have extensive delisted stock coverage and estimate our data is 99% free of survivorship bias. To our knowledge this is the most comprehensive dataset that is free of survivorship bias and readily available. We're continuously working on that last 1%, with the most common issue holding us back being malformed historic electronic records that we are improving our ability to process. What is the table schema? We're glad you asked! Yes, we provide schemas for each table for PostgreSQL, SQLite and MySQL databases. You can find these at the individual table docs page, for example fundamentals . Do you provide a data dictionary for the fields of each table? We do indeed. Please see the descriptions table. # Sharadar

> Nearly 30 years of reference-grade US public company data - fundamentals, EOD stock and fund prices, corporate actions, securities master, institutional holdings, and insider transactions. Point-in-time and survivorship-bias-free. Delivered via REST API or bulk CSV zip download.

Sharadar (https://sharadar.com) is a direct data service for quants, analysts, and builders. Tables are known by descriptive names (`fundamentals`, `stocks`, ...) and by well-known legacy codes (`SF1`, `SEP`, ...) that people search for. Both work in the API and docs. Full product documentation lives under `/docs`.

## Getting started

This is the direct Sharadar API: `https://api.sharadar.com/v1.0`. It is not Nasdaq Data Link. Do not call `data.nasdaq.com` or use the `nasdaqdatalink` / `quandl` libraries with a sharadar.com key.

You need an API key from https://sharadar.com/account after sign-in. If there is no key, or a request returns 401, send the user to https://sharadar.com/subscribe (guest checkout is allowed). Do not invent access.

Pass the key as `api_key` or `apiKey` on the query string, or as header `x-api-key`. Do not ask the user to paste the key into chat or hardcode it.

The documented `test-api-key` only returns the free sample universe (roughly DJIA names such as AAPL). A 403 `Exceeds free tier` means that request is running as free-tier, not as a paid key.

For an entire table, use bulk: add `years=5`, `years=10`, or `years=full` to `GET /data/{table}`. The API responds 302 to a zip. `tickers` and `descriptions` only publish a full snapshot; `years=5` and `years=10` still download that file. Do not page a full table with `limit` and `skip` / `offset`. Use `ticker`, `from`, `to`, and `fields` for slices. Delisted tickers are in the same tables (for example `ticker=TWO` on `/data/stocks`). Dates are calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`); fundamentals also has `calendardate` vs `date`.

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://sharadar.com/docs/intro): Overview of the API and data tables
- [Authentication](https://sharadar.com/docs/auth): API keys and how to attach `api_key` to requests
- [Querying](https://sharadar.com/docs/getting-started): Filters, formats, limits, and common query patterns
- [Bulk Downloads](https://sharadar.com/docs/bulk): Pre-built table zips (5Y / 10Y / full history)
- [FAQs](https://sharadar.com/docs/faqs): Ticker changes, adjustments, survivorship bias, schemas
- Docs also resolve legacy codes as paths (e.g. [/docs/SF1](https://sharadar.com/docs/SF1) -> fundamentals)

## Data tables

Each table has a modern name and, where applicable, a legacy code (same data either way). Legacy codes such as **SF1** and **SEP** are widely searched and remain first-class.

- [Indicator Descriptions (`descriptions`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/descriptions): Field-level data dictionary
- [Fundamentals / SF1 (`fundamentals`, `SF1`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/fundamentals): Company financial statements and fundamentals - also [/docs/SF1](https://sharadar.com/docs/SF1)
- [Stock Prices / SEP (`stocks`, `SEP`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/stocks): EOD OHLCV for US equities (unadjusted, split-adjusted, and fully adjusted) - also [/docs/SEP](https://sharadar.com/docs/SEP)
- [Fund Prices / SFP (`funds`, `SFP`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/funds): EOD prices for funds - also [/docs/SFP](https://sharadar.com/docs/SFP)
- [Daily Fundamentals (`daily`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/daily): Daily fundamental snapshots
- [Price Metrics (`metrics`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/metrics): Price-based metrics
- [Tickers and Metadata (`tickers`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/tickers): Securities master and metadata (`permaticker` is Sharadar's stable security / share-class id)
- [Corporate Actions (`actions`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/actions): Splits, dividends, ticker changes, etc.
- [Material Events (`events`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/events): Material corporate events
- [S&P 500 Constituents (`sp500`)](https://sharadar.com/docs/sp500): Historical S&P 50

## Data-source research: Sharadar and a second daily price source (read 2026-10-17)

**Main finding:** Sharadar now sells and documents its data directly at sharadar.com, with its own API (`api.sharadar.com/v1.0`). Its own guide says "It is not Nasdaq Data Link" and says not to use a sharadar.com key with `nasdaqdatalink` (https://sharadar.com/llms.txt). I couldn't read Nasdaq Data Link's own Sharadar pages: data.nasdaq.com/databases/SEP and /SFA load only an empty page without JavaScript, and docs.data.nasdaq.com redirects to /accesstools. So the Sharadar facts below come from sharadar.com. Whether they also hold for your Data Link subscription is unconfirmed (probe P1).

### Part A — Sharadar

**1. SEP (stock prices, now called `stocks`)** (https://sharadar.com/docs/stocks)
- **Fields:** ticker, date, open, high, low, close, volume, closeadj, closeunadj, lastupdated.
- **Adjustment:**
  - open/high/low/close/volume are adjusted for splits only.
  - `closeadj` is adjusted for splits, cash dividends and spinoffs.
  - `closeunadj` is not adjusted.
- **History and coverage:** history starts December 1997. The table covers "active and delisted US public stocks", about 21,000 tickers. Data is delivered daily at 17:30 and 23:30 ET.
- **Rebuilding other prices:** unadjusted open = open × closeunadj / close. Volume is not adjusted for dividends or spinoffs (https://sharadar.com/docs/faqs).

**2. ACTIONS (`actions`)** (https://sharadar.com/docs/actions)
- **Fields:** date, action, ticker, name, value, contraticker, contraname. History starts January 1998.
- **Action types:** the data dictionary lists 75 (pulled with the public sample key from `https://api.sharadar.com/v1.0/data/descriptions?api_key=test-api-key&table=actiontypes`). They include:
  - split, dividend, spinoff, spinoffdividend
  - tickerchangefrom/tickerchangeto, listed, delisted, voluntarydelisting, regulatorydelisting, bankruptcyliquidation
  - acquisitionby, acquisitioncash, acquisitionstock, acquisitionelectcash/stock, mergerfrom/mergerto, relation, exchangefrom/to, sicchangefrom/to
  - many acquisition variants such as "besteffort", "estimated" and per-currency cash.
- **Meaning of key types:**
  - For `dividend`, value is the cash amount adjusted for splits, and date is the ex-date.
  - For `split`, value is shares held after per share held before.
  - For the delisting types, date is the last trade date.

**3. TICKERS (`tickers`)** (https://sharadar.com/docs/tickers)
- **Fields:** permaticker ("a unique and unchanging identifier for a security (share class)"), isdelisted (Y/N), category, sector, industry, sicsector, famaindustry, firstpricedate, lastpricedate, firstadded, cusips, figi, relatedtickers.
- **Ticker reuse:** when a ticker is reused, "the active company keeps the ticker and the delisted company gets a number appended". When a ticker changes, the history moves to the new ticker (https://sharadar.com/docs/faqs).

**4. SP500 (`sp500`)** (https://sharadar.com/docs/sp500)
- **Contents:** current members, additions and removals with effective dates, plus quarterly snapshots of the index.
- **Fields:** date, action, ticker, name, contraticker, contraname, note. History starts January 1998.
- **Plans:** "Included in Fundamentals, Prices, Bundle", so it is not a separate add-on on sharadar.com.

**5. Access**
- **sharadar.com:** bulk download with `years=5|10|full`, which redirects to a zip file; the docs advise against paging through a whole table (https://sharadar.com/docs/stocks, https://sharadar.com/llms.txt). The default row limit is 10,000 (https://sharadar.com/docs/getting-started). I found no published rate limit.
- **Data Link Python client:** installed with `pip install nasdaq-data-link`. `get_table(..., paginate=True)` reads several pages, and `export_table()` downloads a filtered zip ("`cursor_id` and `paginate` are not supported for exporting"). It retries automatically on HTTP 429 (https://github.com/Nasdaq/data-link-python/blob/main/FOR_ANALYSTS.md, https://github.com/Nasdaq/data-link-python/blob/main/README.md).
- **Data Link rate limits:**
  - Observed directly: an anonymous request returned "anonymous user limit of 50 calls per day" (data.nasdaq.com API).
  - From a search snippet of https://docs.data.nasdaq.com/docs/rate-limits-1, which now redirects so I couldn't read it: about 2,000 calls per 10 minutes for free keys, 5,000 per 10 minutes and 720,000 per day for table subscribers, and 60 per hour for `qopts.export`. Treat these as unverified.

**6. Delisting return**
- Sharadar provides no delisting return. You get the last price, the last trade date, and a delisting action whose value is the final market cap.
- The action type works as a reason code: voluntary, regulatory, bankruptcy/liquidation, acquisition or merger.
- Cash and stock paid per share in an acquisition are in `acquisitioncash` and `acquisitionstock`. The FAQ estimates about 99% coverage and excludes contingent value rights (https://sharadar.com/docs/faqs).

**Open questions for Sharadar (probes):**
- **P1:** Do Data Link's SHARADAR/SEP, ACTIONS and SP500 tables match sharadar.com in fields and action types? Is SP500 part of your Data Link bundle?
- **P2:** How is closeadj computed (dividend factor, multiplicative or additive)? Is it recalculated going back in time?
- **P3:** How is a delisting return derived from the acquisition cash/stock values?
- **P4:** What are the actual rate limits on your Data Link key?
- **P5:** Does SP500 store tickers as they were at the time, or the current renamed ones?

### Part B — Second daily price source

| Source | Price and limits | History | Delisted | Unadjusted, dividends, splits | Terms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EODHD** | Historian plan $19.99/month: 100,000 calls/day, 1,000/min, 30+ years. Free plan: 20 calls/day, 1 year (https://eodhd.com/pricing) | US data from 1962 | Yes: `exchange-symbol-list/US?delisted=1`. Names delisted before 2018 have prices only, no splits or dividends (https://eodhd.com/financial-apis/delisted-stock-companies-data-2) | `close` "as traded — not adjusted", `adjusted_close` for splits and dividends; separate splits and dividends API (https://eodhd.com/financial-apis/api-for-historical-data-and-volumes) | Plans marked "Personal" |
| **Tiingo** | Power plan $30/month: 10,000 requests/hour, 100,000/day, all symbols. Free: 500 symbols/month, 50 requests/hour (https://www.tiingo.com/about/pricing) | 30+ years | Not stated in the docs | Raw close plus adjClose, divCash, splitFactor; adjustment follows the CRSP method (https://www.tiingo.com/documentation/end-of-day) | "Internal use only" |
| **Alpha Vantage** | $49.99/month for 75 requests/min; free is 25/day (https://www.alphavantage.co/premium/) | 25+ years | Delisted lists from 2010 onward, but the docs don't say whether price history exists for delisted symbols | DAILY is raw; DAILY_ADJUSTED (premium) adds adjusted close plus split and dividend events (https://www.alphavantage.co/documentation/) | — |
| **Massive (formerly Polygon)** | Starter $29/month for 5 years of history; 10 years costs $79/month (https://massive.com/pricing) | Too short for 2010 at ≤$50 | — | `adjusted` covers splits only (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/aggregates/custom-bars) | Individual use |
| **Stooq** | stooq.com/db/h/ blocks automated requests behind a JavaScript check, so I couldn't read terms or adjustment rules | — | — | — | Unverified |
| **yfinance** | Unofficial: "not affiliated… with Yahoo"; "Yahoo! finance API is intended for personal use only" (https://github.com/ranaroussi/yfinance/blob/main/README.md) | — | Delisted names are generally missing (not documented) | — | Fragile |

**Recommendation: EODHD Historian at $19.99/month.** It is the only candidate within budget that documents all of the following: delisted US tickers, raw close, adjusted close, a splits and dividends API, and 30+ years of history. Tiingo Power ($30) is the fallback; it has the cleanest fields and CRSP-style adjustment, but its docs say nothing about delisted coverage.

For the 1bp check, don't compare one vendor's adjusted close directly to the other's. EODHD says adjusted closes "are recomputed, not stored", and the two vendors may adjust differently. Instead, build daily returns from each vendor's raw close, dividends and splits, and compare those. The 0.5% check compares raw close to Sharadar's `closeunadj`.

**Open questions for Part B (probes):**
- **P6:** How do EODHD symbols map to Sharadar tickers for renamed or reused symbols? EODHD returns an empty series under the old name, e.g. FB.US.
- **P7:** Do the 2010–2017 delisted names have dividends and splits (EODHD says prices only)? That limits the return check for those names.
- **P8:** Does the second source actually cover at least 50% of S&P 500 member-days? Measure it.
- **P9:** Does Tiingo have delisted coverage?
- **P10:** Do EODHD's or Tiingo's personal-use terms allow storing the data locally for cross-checks?
